title: What a Diff'rence a Day Makes

meta.title: Who originally recorded "What a Diff'rence a Day Makes"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Dinah Washington's 1959 hit was a cover. Maria Grever wrote the song in 1934 as "Cuando vuelva a tu lado" - and which 1934 record came first is disputed.
meta.ogTitle: Who originally recorded 'What a Diff'rence a Day Makes'?
meta.ogDescription: Not a 1959 original: the song is Maria Grever's 1934 "Cuando vuelva a tu lado", recorded twice that year before Dinah Washington was a teenager.

answer.label: Not a Dinah Washington original — but the “first recording” is contested
answer.originalArtistDates: Active mid-1930s · Latin dance orchestra led by trumpeter Pedro Via, recording for Victor in New York
answer.sourceLine: Dinah Washington’s 1959 Mercury single is so completely hers that the song is routinely treated as starting there. It does not: María Grever wrote it in 1934 as the Spanish song “Cuando vuelva a tu lado,” and Stanley Adams supplied the English lyric the same year. The usual correction — that Orquesta Pedro Vía recorded it first — is where our research parts company with the reference books: the Victor master was cut in New York on 10 December 1934, while the Dorsey Brothers’ Decca side with Bob Crosby was already on wax from 29 October 1934. Vía’s is the earliest Spanish-language recording we can document, not demonstrably the earliest recording of the song.

original.heading: Who recorded it first
original.label: Victor
original.released: Recorded in New York on 10 December 1934 in Victor’s Studio 2 (matrix BS-86425) and issued as a 10-inch Victor 78, catalogue number 32361, under the Spanish title “Cuando vuelva a tu lado.” Victor’s own ledgers already carried “What a diff’rence a day made” as a subtitle.
original.charted: Did not chart. It was a Spanish-language dance side aimed at a Latin catalogue market, not the American pop lists.
original.cover: Dinah Washington’s 1959 Mercury single reached number 8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 4 R&B, won the Grammy for Best Rhythm and Blues Performance and entered the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1998.

María Grever; English lyric by Stanley Adams

trail: UCSB’s Discography of American Historical Recordings ↗ reconstructs the session from Victor’s blue history card and ledgers: 10 December 1934, Studio 2, New York, with Pedro Vía on trumpet and leading, a vocalist logged as Chiquito, and Alfredo Cibelli directing.
The Internet Archive’s catalogue record for the digitised Decca 283 A ↗ dates the Dorsey Brothers’ English recording, with Bob Crosby singing, to 29 October 1934 — before the Victor session.
MusicBrainz ↗ holds the composition as a Spanish-language work credited to María Grever as both composer and lyricist, ISWC T-070.028.704-2.

authors.name: Orquesta Pedro Vía
authors.heading: Orquesta Pedro Vía
authors.metaLine: Latin dance orchestra · recorded for Victor in New York, 1934
authors.bio: Pedro Vía led a small Latin dance band — violin, bass, trumpet, guitar, two pianos and traps — that cut sides for Victor in New York in 1934. On 10 December that year the group recorded María Grever’s “Cuando vuelva a tu lado” in Victor’s Studio 2, with a male vocal refrain credited on the ledger simply as Chiquito and Alfredo Cibelli directing the date. The master, BS-86425, was issued on the 10-inch Victor 32361. It is the earliest recording of the song we could document under its Spanish title.

authors.name: Dinah Washington
authors.heading: Dinah Washington
authors.metaLine: 1924–1963 · American jazz, blues and R&B singer
authors.bio: Born Ruth Lee Jones, Washington was one of the most popular Black women on record in the 1950s and called herself the Queen of the Blues. Her 1959 Mercury version of the song was her first top-ten pop hit, reaching number 8 on the Billboard Hot 100, and it won the Grammy for Best Rhythm and Blues Performance; it entered the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1998. The reading is definitive enough that most listeners assume she introduced the song. The only error in that assumption is chronological.

authors.name: María Grever
authors.heading: María Grever
authors.bio: Grever was the first Mexican woman composer to win an international audience, and this is the song she is remembered for. She wrote both words and music of “Cuando vuelva a tu lado” in 1934; MusicBrainz credits her as composer and lyricist of the work, and Victor’s own ledgers name her on both counts. The English lyric that carried the song into the American songbook was written separately by Stanley Adams (1907–1994), later the long-serving president of ASCAP. Grever died in 1951, eight years before the recording that made the song famous.

misattribution.heading: What’s actually true
misattribution.intro: This one has two errors stacked on top of each other — the popular one, and a smaller one in the usual correction.

items.who: Dinah Washington originated the song in 1959
items.why: Her Mercury single is a cover. The song was written and recorded in 1934, and Washington was born in 1924.

items.who: María Grever, with English lyrics by Stanley Adams
items.why: Victor’s ledgers and MusicBrainz both credit Grever as composer and lyricist of the Spanish original; Adams wrote the English lyric, published late in 1934.

items.who: Orquesta Pedro Vía recorded it first, in 1934
items.why: Vía’s Victor master was cut on 10 December 1934. The Dorsey Brothers’ Decca side with Bob Crosby is dated 29 October 1934, and an English recording by Jimmie Ague is reported earlier still, though we could not confirm its date.
It is the earliest recording of the song under its Spanish title that we could confirm against a discographical source.

misattribution.truthLine: Washington did not originate it — but neither, on the dates we can verify, did the record usually named as the original.

context.heading: Why the 1959 record swallowed the 1934 ones
lead: The song had a busy 1934 and almost nobody remembers it. Grever wrote it in Spanish, Stanley Adams put an English lyric on it and it was published late that year, and within months there were competing records on two labels in two languages — a Decca side by the Dorsey Brothers with a young Bob Crosby singing, a Victor side by Orquesta Pedro Vía, and, reportedly, an earlier English version by the Cleveland singer Jimmie Ague. None of them became the song’s permanent address.

Twenty-five years is a long time for a standard to sit around waiting, and what Washington did with it in 1959 was less a cover than a repossession. The Mercury record won a Grammy, put her in the pop top ten for the first time, and fixed a tempo and a mood that every later version answers to. Once a song has a definitive performance, its earlier life stops being audible — which is how a Mexican composer’s 1934 bolero ends up filed under American R&B.
detailsBody: 1934 — María Grever writes “Cuando vuelva a tu lado” in Spanish.
1934 — Stanley Adams writes the English lyric; the song is published late in the year under the title “What a Diff’rence a Day Made.”
29 October 1934 — the Dorsey Brothers’ Orchestra records the English version with a vocal chorus by Bob Crosby; issued on Decca 283 A, matrix 38914.
10 December 1934 — Orquesta Pedro Vía records the Spanish original in Victor’s New York Studio 2, matrix BS-86425, issued on Victor 32361.
1959 — Dinah Washington records it for Mercury; the single reaches number 8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and wins a Grammy for Best Rhythm and Blues Performance.
1998 — Washington’s recording is inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.
context.pull: The song was already on two labels in two languages before Washington was ten years old.
